- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/default-organization-invariant.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66a3008ed6b86571705b53873431e89be0e392de` — the merge of head `431216f3acf30abd62f8e2243ce98ae16c45af60` into base `150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66a3008ed6b86571705b53873431e89be0e392de && git checkout 66a3008ed6b86571705b53873431e89be0e392de
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 431216f3acf30abd62f8e2243ce98ae16c45af60 && git checkout -B drift-repro 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 && git merge --no-ff 431216f3acf30abd62f8e2243ce98ae16c45af60

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67f99e580f19175283a8fec68d59dcea30574744`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23189 (body, triage `6140079217`, claim `6140412835`, report `6141438413`, amendment `6141484443`), PR #23203 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` at the head above) and the head's 40 check-runs (34 success, 6 skipped). Read-only: no checkout, build, test or gate re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Posture judgment in `IdentityObjectsPlugin.start()` — right.** The invariant runs only when `postureInForce(ctx)` reads `single`: the `tenancy` service's posture when a host registered one, else `resolveTenancyPosture()`. `AuthPlugin.start()` reads `this.tenancy?.posture`, the service its own `init()` registers (`providesServices = ['auth', 'tenancy']`), so in the full kernel "service, else requested" collapses to the same judge; `AppPlugin.organizationWallActive()` is literally service-else-requested, read live per call. Matching `AppPlugin` is the right choice: the organization must precede that plugin's inline seed, so the two decisions have to agree, and without `AuthPlugin` nothing computes a degraded posture, so the request is the only fact. Pinned in both directions (a host `tenancy` service overrides the request). One divergence, not a defect: `AuthPlugin` guards against an engine without `find`/`insert`; this plugin does not, and cannot reach that case because `com.objectstack.engine.objectql` is its hard dependency. `resolveTenancyPosture()` throwing on an unrecognised value fails the boot from `start()`, the same fail-fast `AuthPlugin.init()` already applies.

2. **Refused before, admitted now — right, a declared-contract restoration with its citation.** Under `single`, seeds and system writes on tenant-scoped objects that hit the D9 `no-organization` refusal in the reduced kernel are now derived and stamped. ADR-0131 D3 declares the Default Organization "load-bearing: it exists before the first write that needs an owner", "created before application seed datasets load under `single`", "a failure becomes a boot error"; D9 derives the owner under `single`. The engine's own refusal text names the refused condition as a write that "ran in a composition that never booted the auth plugin" — the reduced kernel was that composition while registering the object that makes D9 refuse. Nothing is admitted beyond D3: several organizations with none `default` still refuse (`ambiguous`, logged at warn exactly as `AuthPlugin` logs it), walled postures are untouched, and `ambiguous` creates no row. The citation (ADR-0131 D3, quoted through `default-organization-invariant.ts`) is present in the claim, the PR body and the changeset.

3. **Admitted before, refused now — wrong as declared: this half is a narrowing.** (i) A composition that mounts `createIdentityObjectsPlugin()` and publishes its driver only after `bootstrap()` booted on the previous release and now fails in Phase 2 with `No driver available for object 'sys_organization'`. (ii) A kit that inserted its own organization row after boot now holds two under `single`, and every system write naming no organization is refused `ambiguous-organization` (`resolveSystemWriteOrganization` derives only at exactly one row; where a legacy unique index on `slug` exists the kit's insert fails as a duplicate instead). The `runas-system-stamping` rig's removed insert was an ADR-0131-compliant arrangement, not a lean on the defect: its deleted comment cited D3 and it held exactly one organization before any system write. The published prescription for this plugin states no driver-at-boot requirement — `.changeset/22074-auth-identity-objects-plugin.md` ("Usage. `await kernel.use(createIdentityObjectsPlugin())` after `ObjectQLPlugin`"; "It registers objects only"), and `SecurityPlugin`'s refusal text that names `createIdentityObjectsPlugin()` as the remedy. In-repo population: 2 of the 3 pre-existing consumer rigs of this plugin went red. (iii) `multi` / walled postures: unchanged — `start()` returns before any read; pinned for `group`, `isolated`, and the runtime pin's `isolated` control (no row, inline seed left to the per-organization replay). (iv) Mounting beside `AuthPlugin`: unchanged — `init()` is untouched and the refusal is pinned at `init()` on a real kernel. The design is the one triage directed and is right; what is wrong is the declaration (②).

4. **`AppPlugin.optionalDependencies` gains `com.objectstack.auth.identity-objects` — right.** ADR-0116 D1 order-if-present: `resolvePluginOrder` hoists a composed name and skips an absent one over the kernel's plugin map, whatever the `use()` order, and Phase 2 iterates the same `orderedPlugins` as Phase 1, so start order follows. No cycle: the identity plugin's edges are `com.objectstack.engine.objectql` (hard) and `com.objectstack.auth` (optional); `AuthPlugin`'s are objectql (hard) and `com.objectstack.service.settings` (optional); nothing declares an edge towards an `AppPlugin`, whose kernel name is the app's manifest id. The only reordering it can cause is the intended one (identity objects init and start before an app that was listed ahead of them), and no in-repo plugin needs to sit between the two. The measured necessity (commit `5373c9776b`: 2 of 4 pin cases red without the edge) is accepted. The field keeps its type; a changed array literal is not a surface change.

5. **Public surface — right, not a widening.** The built `.d.ts` gains `start(ctx: PluginContext): Promise[void]` on the exported class `IdentityObjectsPlugin` (bracket spelling here only, to keep angle brackets out of this record). `Plugin.start?` in `packages/core/src/types.ts` is the kernel contract's existing optional lifecycle member: a consumer typed against `Plugin` sees nothing new, one typed against the class sees that optional member made concrete. No new export, option, type or error code; `postureInForce` is module-private; the new imports are types plus `resolveTenancyPosture` from a dependency `auth-plugin.ts` already uses. The dev's H3 is accepted on the source reading; nothing was built here.

6. **The two `service-automation` rig changes — fixtures this change legitimately breaks, and at the same time the evidence of the consumer break the release must announce.** They are the in-repo sample of the accept set that narrowed (①.3), fixed in the PR that breaks them, which is the right practice; what they show is the shape ② has to carry.

7. **Checked, unchanged:** `os migrate plan` / `apply` mount `createIdentityObjectsPlugin()` through `composeProviderForDeclarations`, whose proxy substitutes `start()`, so a declaration boot still writes no organization. `@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack` mounts `AuthPlugin` and is outside the change.

### ② Semver level

**Judged wrong: the level markers do not carry what the diff publishes.** The changeset grades `patch` for both packages, declares `Clause-②: no` with no arm, carries no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition — and then carries a consumer migration paragraph ("If your test kit mounts `createIdentityObjectsPlugin()` … Otherwise the boot fails … drop that insert"). ①.3 is a narrowing of the published accept set: compositions that booted on the previous release, and that followed the published prescription, are refused at boot, and the fix is on the consumer's side. Two landed siblings declared exactly this class as BREAKING under the launch-window convention: `.changeset/22074-security-identity-objects-boot-refusal.md` ("a kernel that booted before is refused at boot" — `minor`, `**BREAKING**`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) and #23171 / `.changeset/23142-settings-anonymous-floor.md` (restoring an ADR floor that refuses callers served before — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `minor`, bang summary, banner, marker). Under the window the level is not the carrier; the banner and the disposition are the only signal a consumer gets, and this changeset has neither, so a kit that stops booting would find the change filed under patch fixes.

Gate verdicts, read off the head's check-runs: `Check Changeset` step 13 "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" — success; step 15 "Guard against accidental major bumps (launch window)" — success. Both greens are conditional on the declaration as written: the ADR-0087 gate saw no breaking signal (no `major`, no banner, no bang, no narrowing arm) and the level axis stood down on `no` with no arm. With the corrected arm both gates demand exactly what the fix below supplies. `.changeset/pre.json` is in `pre` mode; the launch-window convention still ships breaking as `minor` (the sibling precedent, same day).

**Exact fix (a patch round, no design change):**
- `.changeset/23189-identity-objects-default-organization.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': minor` (the narrowing lives there; `'@objectstack/runtime': patch` may stay — the level axis reads that as `discharged`, exit 0); first body line a bang summary, `fix(plugin-auth)!: IdentityObjectsPlugin keeps the single posture's Default Organization at boot`; the declaration line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` followed by the same restoration citation; a `**BREAKING**` banner naming what is refused (a kit whose driver is published after `bootstrap()`; a kit that inserts its own organization row) and what is unchanged (walled postures, the refusal beside `AuthPlugin`, every composition that publishes its driver before boot); an `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …` disposition in the HTML-comment form the sibling changeset `22074-security-identity-objects-boot-refusal.md` carries (no spec key, export, option, config field or stored shape moves; the remedy is a composition edit no ledger entry can derive); keep the existing migration paragraph as the FROM → TO text.
- PR #23203 body, the `Clause-②` line: `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — restores ADR-0131 D3's Default Organization boot invariant in the reduced kernel; a composition that publishes its driver after bootstrap() is now refused at boot, and a kit's hand-inserted organization row is refused as ambiguous; no published schema or export moves.` PR title: `fix(plugin-auth)!: …`.
- The claim's `Clause-②: no` (`6140412835`, kept by `6141484443`) is the seat's line to amend to `no (narrowing)`, not the dev's.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Widened file surface — accepted.** `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (one `optionalDependencies` entry plus docblock) and its runtime pin: same defect class, measured necessary (①.4), a mechanical copy of the existing `com.objectstack.auth` entry; the claim amendment `6141484443` accepts it and records `packages/runtime` as `domain:cli`. The lane declaration lives outside this review's inputs and is not re-verified here. The two `service-automation` rigs are in scope as the fixtures the change breaks.
- **Harness-only ablation mutation — accepted.** The runtime pin's logger `silent` to `warn` was a visibility aid, restored; the blob the diff adds for that file is `c921f402c0`, the pre-mutation hash the report names, so the committed pin is the un-mutated one.
- **Merge commit `67f99e580f` without the trailer pair — accepted, no action.** `scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs`, the pre-push gate, pins a trailer-less `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'` commit as clean by design; the squash landing drops it.
- **Stale "Its one caller is `AuthPlugin`" header in `default-organization-invariant.ts` — accepted as deferred.** The module is not re-exported from the barrel (unpublished bytes); the claim declared the file read-only; the seat records it on its seat post. The patch round this record owes may fold the one-sentence fix in if the seat lifts the read-only line; not a condition of PASS.
- **Three posture judges — answered: an observation, not a condition.** This plugin's judge equals `AppPlugin`'s (①.1), which is the pair that must agree. `SecurityPlugin` (tenancy service, else `org-scoping` present means `isolated` else `single`, injected into the engine) differs only for a walled request in a reduced kernel without `org-scoping`: no organization is created and the engine refuses system writes loudly either way. Pre-existing, outside this diff; escalated to the seat as a note, no card owed by this PR.
- **`open_questions`: none.** The 403s on cloud reads change nothing: the `AppPlugin` edge makes the fix independent of `use()` order, and cloud's pin bump is cloud's step.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23189-identity-objects-default-org`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FzQy26KznSa5j2gnf3AzsE`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
